 Medvedev vs. Cobolli live updates: ATP Finals 2026 latest with night session match underway
 Follow live updates as Russia's Medvedev faces Italy's Cobolli in Turin today. Live Blog Chat George Ramsay November 16, 2026 at 3:30 PM EST Cobolli plays a forehand return against Medvedev   Getty Images Max Mathews · Staff Writer, Live Medvedev vs. Cobolli: ATP Finals latest
 The ATP Finals continue with the second day of action in Turin, Italy today. 
 Russian Daniil Medvedev (4) faces Italian Flavio Cobolli (5) in their first match of the year-end tournament.
 How to watch: Tennis Channel (U.S.); Sky Sports (UK)
 Tune in with Fubo (U.S. and Canada, try for free )
 Join the discussion at the top of the page or email : live@theathletic.com 
 4 D. Medvedev Serving 30 5 5 F. Cobolli 0 5 LIVE View all Tennis Matches SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Advertisement
 November 16, 2026 at 3:30 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Cobolli saves more break points and levels
   Getty Images Medvedev (4) *4-4 Cobolli (5) 
 Medvedev's first serve is at 85 percent so far, helping him to keep his service games brief.
 Can he put more pressure on the Cobolli serve? 
 It looks like it as the fourth seed's skidding ground shots put him 0-30 ahead, then a simple volley sent long by Cobolli opens up three break points. 
 But the Italian saves all of them! A 29-shot rally at 30-40 ends with Cobolli passing Medvedev thanks to a crisp backhand. 
 From there, the fourth seed holds with a ripping forehand. He's saved five break points already this match
 November 16, 2026 at 3:19 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Cobolli's forehand starts to deliver
   Getty Images Medvedev (4) *3-3 Cobolli (5) 
 Medvedev has found a nice rhythm with his serve early on in this contest, holding to love for a 3-2 lead. 
 Cobolli responds with a pair of enormous forehands on his service game, the second an absolute rocket down the line. 
 A backhand volley at full stretch completes the hold and we remain level in this first set.
 November 16, 2026 at 3:14 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Cobolli saves two break points
   Getty Images Medvedev (4) *2-2 Cobolli (5) 
 Lots of support, obviously, for Cobolli tonight — including from his peers. 
 Fellow Italian Matteo Berrettini is watching from the stands and gets a big cheers when he appears on the big screen inside the stadium.
 A hold to 15 for Medvedev in his second service game but Cobolli finds himself in trouble when he nets a backhand, giving the fourth seed two break points. 
 One is saved, then another with a serve out wide. And Cobolli's serve ultimately sees out the game as he seals the hold with an ace. 
 First hurdle overcome for the fifth seed. 
 November 16, 2026 at 3:05 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Comfortable holds for both players
   Getty Images Medvedev (4) *1-1 Cobolli (5) 
 No problem for Medvedev in the opening game of the match as he holds thanks to a couple of aces. 
 It's straightforward for Cobolli, too, as he pumps an ace of his own down the middle of the court to complete a hold. 
 November 16, 2026 at 2:58 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live We're underway!
   Getty Images Medvedev (4) 0-0 Cobolli (5) 
 We're up and running in the Inalpi Arena, with Medvedev serving first. 
 SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Advertisement
 November 16, 2026 at 2:58 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Medvedev leads the head-to-head
 This is the fourth meeting between these two, with Medvedev leading the head-to-head 2-1.
 The last meeting at this year's Madrid Open, though, went Cobolli 's way in three sets. 
 November 16, 2026 at 2:53 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live The players are out on the court
   Getty Images Pre-match presentations out the way, let's now turn our attention to tonight's match between Medvedev and Cobolli .
 The players are now out on the court, with Italian Cobolli first and greeted by a big roar from the home fans in Turin. 
 A headphoned, game-faced Medvedev follows. This one will be underway soon. 
 November 16, 2026 at 2:50 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live   Getty Images Here is Alexander Zverev with the year-end No. 1 trophy.
 He defeated Rafael Jódar in his opener yesterday and will be back on this court to face Ben Shelton tomorrow.
 November 16, 2026 at 2:45 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Zverev: ‘Biggest achievement’ to be year-end No. 1
 Before tonight's match between Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli gets underway, Alexander Zverev has been out on the court receiving the year-end No. 1 trophy.
 Here's what the two-time Grand Slam winner said just now about topping the rankings. 
 💬 “It’s a great honor to be holding this trophy, to be part of this presentation and this celebration. Last year playing this tournament, I thought yes, maybe I could win a Grand Slam, maybe I could do well during the year, but I didn’t even imagine that I could stand here holding this trophy. 
 “To be the year-end world No. 1, it’s the most special thing, I think it’s the biggest achievement of my career to be holding this trophy.” 
 November 16, 2026 at 2:38 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live The ATP Finals contenders
 If you want to read Matthew Futterman 's preview of this year's ATP Finals — and his assessment of the contenders for the crown — then you can do so by heading here .

 November 16, 2026 at 2:34 PM EST James Hansen · Senior Managing Editor, Tennis A strange stat behind Cobolli's ATP Finals appearance
   Getty Images Flavio Cobolli , 24, enters the ATP Finals as world No. 6, despite having lost more points than he has won this year. He is the first player to finish in the top 10 with such a record since the data became available in 1991, as first analyzed by Jeff Sackmann of Tennis Abstract.
 The tennis scoring system is known for its ability to create statistical quirks. Players can win individual matches despite losing more points than their opponent, and even the most dominant ones in history win just a little over half of the points they play in their career. 20-time Grand Slam champion Roger Federer turned that into a philosophy for a commencement speech; it is the bedrock of a sport that has no clock. But the curious case of Cobolli cannot be explained by the scoring system alone. How Cobolli wins, and the player that he is, contribute too.
 In 2026, Cobolli has won 60 percent of his matches, with a 36-24 record. He has won 55 percent of his sets (90-73). But he has won just 49.8 percent of his points, and a similar percentage of his games.
 For 2026, Cobolli is 7-1 when he has won between 49 percent and 51 percent of points played. Just nine of his 36 wins have seen him win 55 percent of points or more, but 16 of his 24 losses have seen him win 45 percent of points or fewer.
 He has five wins with under 50 percent of points won in 2026. The rest of the field at the ATP Finals has nine between them. Cobolli is also 19-12 in tiebreaks this year, a 61 percent record that would put him among the elite if sustained for an entire career. On average, tiebreak results hew closely to a player’s results in normal sets (55 percent won this year for Cobolli) so it’s unlikely that he will sustain that record.
 The numbers offer ballast to an eye-test theory of Cobolli that has become clearer and clearer since his ascendance in the sport: he has one of the widest gaps between his top level and his bottom level on the ATP Tour. When he is good, he is very good; when he is clutch, he is very clutch; and when he is not good, he is not good at all.

 November 16, 2026 at 2:24 PM EST Matthew Futterman · Senior Tennis Writer Player in focus: Flavio Cobolli
   Getty Images No player will be more overjoyed to be playing in Turin than French Open finalist Flavio Cobolli , who will be making his debut at the ATP Finals in front of a home crowd. With Sinner absent, the Italian faithful will throw their support behind him.
 Still, if there were one player in the field who might be better served skipping than playing right now, it might be him. 
 Cobolli has largely been running on fumes since July. He made the quarterfinals at Wimbledon and the semifinals of the Cincinnati Open, but it’s been pretty ugly other than that. He has a high ceiling, but one of the lowest floors on the tour, which is why he's the first player since 1991 to finish in the top 10 while losing over 50 percent of the points he has played all year.
 At the Vienna Open, he retired from the first set of his second match with a strained muscle in his left leg. He then withdrew from the Paris Masters to rest for Turin. If he makes it, he will light up the arena in every match he plays — just not necessarily with his tennis.
 November 16, 2026 at 2:16 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Medvedev's ATP Finals record
   Getty Images Daniil Medvedev is one of only two former ATP Finals champions in the field this year, alongside Alexander Zverev, having defeated Dominic Thiem in the showpiece match in 2020. 
 He has a 12-11 record in the tournament and is 2-4 against the field this year.
 2025 — Did not qualify
 2024 — Round-robin
 2023 — Semifinals
 2022 — Round-robin
 2021 — Final
 2020 — Win
 2019 — Round-robin
 November 16, 2026 at 2:10 PM EST Matthew Futterman · Senior Tennis Writer Player in focus: Daniil Medvedev
   Getty Images No matter how well Daniil Medvedev does in Turin, he’s got to be the ATP comeback story of the year.
 Medvedev’s career was headed in the wrong direction in 2025. He lost in the second round of the Australian Open, and then in the first round of the next three Grand Slams. His serve had ceased to be a weapon. It looked like the always entertaining Medvedev show, which had brought him a Grand Slam title and the world No. 1 ranking, was coming to a close, in a fit of on-court outbursts and worsening losses.
 Lately, though, Medvedev has been showing signs of his old prowess. He’s been hot this fall, winning two tournaments and making the semis or better at every tournament he played until he got to the Paris Masters, where he seemed to run out of gas. 
 Given where he was headed at the end of last year, making it to Turin is a big victory for Medvedev, who comes in as the world No. 5.
 November 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM EST Nancy Froston · Senior Writer, Live Andreeva crowned WTA Finals champion
   Getty Images Away from Turin, yesterday saw Mirra Andreeva defeat Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to be crowned WTA champion at Indian Wells.
 It marked Andreeva's first WTA Finals title and the 19-year-old became the youngest winner of the event in 22 years.
 She is up to second in the world rankings behind Elena Rybakina. 
 You can read Ava Wallace 's report on the match here . 
 SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Advertisement
 November 16, 2026 at 1:50 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Last year's tournament
   Getty Images Jannik Sinner won a second straight ATP Finals title on home soil in Turin last year, defeating rival Carlos Alcaraz 7-6(4), 7-5 in the final.
 Sinner won all of his matches on the way to the title and closed out the year with two Grand Slam titles and a 91 percent win-rate.
 The Italian is absent from this year's tournament as he continues his recovery from a right knee injury. 
 November 16, 2026 at 1:40 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Coming up tomorrow
   Getty Images There are two more matches scheduled to take place tomorrow at the ATP Finals.
 Arthur Fils (6) vs. Rafael Jódar (8) — not before 8 a.m. ET / 1 p.m. GMT
 Alexander Zverev (1) vs. Ben Shelton (3) — not before 2:30 p.m. ET / 7:30 p.m. GMT
 Those will both be covered live on The Athletic so be sure to join us then. 
 November 16, 2026 at 1:30 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live What happened earlier today
   Getty Images Spain's Carlos Alcaraz began his pursuit of a first ATP Finals title — the biggest trophy he is yet to win — with a comfortable 6-2, 6-2 victory against USA's Frances Tiafoe earlier today. 
 Having missed much of this season through injury, Alcaraz came into the tournament in Turin off the back of victories in Vienna and Paris, putting him in a strong position to capture the title. 
 His dominant victory against Tiafoe, which took only 70 minutes, was a statement of intent to the rest of the field. 
 November 16, 2026 at 1:20 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live What happened yesterday
   Getty Images ATP Finals action got underway yesterday with American Ben Shelton getting off to a winning start having recorded three defeats in this competition last year. 
 He defeated France's Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 in the tournament opener before Germany's Alexander Zverev , the top seed, overcame Rafael Jódar 6-4, 6-4 in the second match of the day.
